genre.d: a kind of story or book
genre.ex: My favorite genre is funny stories.

folktale.d: an old story that people told again and again for a long, long time
folktale.ex: Grandma told me a folktale about a clever fox.

essential.d: the big question we think about while we read
essential.ex: Our Essential Question is on the board.

work.d: to do a job or try hard to make something happen
work.ex: We work together to clean the classroom.

good.ex: Sharing your snack is a good idea.

way.d: how you do something; also the road you take to go somewhere
way.ex: My dad showed me the way to the park.

solve.d: to find the answer to a problem

problem.d: something that is wrong or hard that you need to fix
problem.ex: My bike has a problem. The tire is flat.

read.d: to look at words and understand them
read.ex: I read a book before bed.

group.ex: A group of ducks swims in the pond.

animal.d: a living thing that can move, like a dog, a bird or a snake
animal.ex: My favorite animal is the panda.

bully.d: someone who is mean and scares or hurts others again and again
bully.ex: The bully took his ball, so he told the teacher.

pictures.ex: She drew a picture of her cat.

anaya.d: the writer of this story; he wrote many stories about New Mexico

diaz.d: the artist who made the pictures for this story
diaz.ex: David Diaz painted the bright pictures in this book.

roadrunner.d: a bird from the desert that runs very fast on long legs; in this story he is the hero
roadrunner.ex: The roadrunner ran across the sand.

dance.d: to move your body to music; a dance is the moves you make
dance.ex: We dance at my sister's birthday party.

dancer.ex: The dancer spins on one foot.

hiss.d: to make a long "sss" sound, like a snake
hiss.ex: The cat hissed at the dog.

snake.d: a long animal with no legs that moves on the ground
snake.ex: We saw a green snake in the grass.

slither.d: to move by sliding the body from side to side, like a snake
slither.ex: The snake slithered under the rock.

hole.d: an empty space in the ground or in something
hole.ex: The rabbit jumped into its hole.

side.ex: We walked on the side of the road.

road.d: a long, hard path where people walk, ride or drive
road.ex: Look both ways before you cross the road.

bare.d: to show your teeth to look scary
bare.ex: The angry dog bared its teeth.

fang.d: a long, sharp tooth of a snake or other animal
fang.ex: A snake has two sharp fangs.

frighten.ex: The loud thunder frightened my little brother.

family.d: a mother, a father and their children

walk.d: to move on your feet, not fast
walk.ex: I walk to school with my friend.

cornfield.ex: The cornfield is green and tall.

mother.d: a woman who has a child; mom

throw.d: to make something fly through the air with your hand; threw = past of throw
throw.ex: He threw the ball to his dog.

basketful.d: as much as a basket can hold
basketful.ex: Grandma picked a basketful of apples.

corn.d: a tall plant with yellow seeds that we eat

air.d: the space above the ground; what we breathe
air.ex: The kids threw their hats in the air.

children.ex: The children play in the park.

freeze.d: to stop moving and stand very still; froze = past of freeze
freeze.ex: The kids froze when the music stopped.

fright.d: a sudden feeling of being very scared

father.d: a man who has a child; dad
father.ex: My father makes pancakes on Sunday.

call.d: to shout to someone so they come; also to give a name

come.d: to move toward a person or place; came = past of come
come.ex: My dog comes when I call him.

run.d: to move very fast on your feet; ran = past of run

threaten.d: to say or show that you will hurt someone
threaten.ex: The big dog threatened the cat by growling.

take.d: to get or carry something with your hands; also to go a way; took = past of take
take.ex: I take my lunch to school.

path.d: a small, narrow way to walk
path.ex: We walked on a path in the forest.

king.d: a man who rules a country; here: the boss who says what everyone must do
king.ex: The king wore a gold crown.

boast.d: to talk too proudly about yourself

use.d: to do something with a thing; to go on a road

permission.ex: I asked for permission to go outside.

evening.d: the time at the end of the day, before night
evening.ex: We play outside in the evening.

people.ex: Many people are at the market.

village.ex: My grandpa lives in a quiet village.

gather.d: to come together in one place; also to pick up and collect
gather.ex: The class gathered around the teacher.

speak.d: to say words; spoke = past of speak
speak.ex: She spoke to her teacher after class.

elder.d: the older, wise people of a group
elder.ex: The elders tell stories to the children.

afraid.ex: My sister is afraid of the dark.

bite.d: to cut with your teeth; bitten = when teeth have cut you; a bite = cut with teeth
bite.ex: Be careful, that dog might bite.

protest.d: to say strongly that something is not fair

act.ex: He acts like a baby when he is tired.

belong.d: to be someone's; "belongs to him" = it is his
belong.ex: This red bag belongs to me.

agree.d: to think the same as someone else
agree.ex: We all agreed to play tag.

following.d: next; the one that comes after
following.ex: We went to the zoo the following day.

morning.d: the early part of the day
morning.ex: I eat breakfast in the morning.

sacredmountain.d: in this story, the special holy mountain where Desert Woman lives
sacredmountain.ex: Desert Woman lives on Sacred Mountain.

desertwoman.d: in this story, a wise, kind woman with special powers who made the desert animals

live.d: to have your home in a place; lived = past of live

create.ex: She created a robot from boxes.

desert.d: a very dry, hot place with lots of sand and little rain
desert.ex: Cactus plants grow in the desert.

help.d: to make something easier for someone
help.ex: I help my mom carry the bags.

neighbor.ex: Our neighbor has a big dog.

visit.d: to go to see a person or place

go.d: to move from one place to another; went = past of go
go.ex: We go to the park on Saturday.

field.d: a big open piece of land where crops grow
field.ex: The farmer works in the field.

impossible.d: cannot happen or cannot be done
impossible.ex: It is impossible to touch the sky.

think.d: to use your mind; thought = past of think

long.d: big from one end to the other; also lasting a lot of time
long.ex: The giraffe has a long neck.

time.d: minutes, hours and days; "for a long time" = for many minutes or hours
time.ex: We waited a long time for the bus.

like_v.d: to enjoy something or think it is good; "did not like to" = did not want to

interfere.d: to get into other people's business when they did not ask you
interfere.ex: Don't interfere when your friends are playing their game.

know.d: to have something in your mind; knew = past of know

solution.ex: We found a solution: we share the toy!

finally.d: at last, after a long time

dress.d: wearing clothes; "dressed in a gown" = wearing a gown
dress.ex: She was dressed in a pink dress for the party.

flowing.d: long and moving softly, like water
flowing.ex: She had a long, flowing dress.

gown.ex: The princess wore a long gown.

travel.d: to go from one place to another, often far away
travel.ex: We traveled to the beach by train.

summer.d: the hottest season of the year
summer.ex: We swim a lot in summer.

cloud.d: a white or gray thing in the sky made of tiny drops of water
cloud.ex: A big white cloud is in the sky.

across.d: from one side to the other side
across.ex: The duck swam across the pond.

sleep.d: to rest with your eyes closed; slept = past of sleep

shade.d: a cool, dark place where the sun does not shine
shade.ex: We sat in the shade of a big tree.

ledge.d: a flat, narrow shelf of rock on the side of a hill or cliff
ledge.ex: A bird sat on a rock ledge.

strike.d: to hit fast and hard; struck = past of strike
strike.ex: The snake can strike very fast.

place.d: to put something in a special spot
place.ex: I placed the cup on the table.

rattle.d: a thing that makes a shaking noise; to rattle = to make that noise

tip.d: the very end of something long and thin
tip.ex: There is ink on the tip of the pen.

tail.d: the long part at the back of an animal's body

rattlesnake.d: a snake with a rattle at the end of its tail that shakes to warn others

warning.d: something that tells you to be careful
warning.ex: The sign is a warning: "Wet floor!"

convinced.ex: I was convinced I was right.

right.d: correct; also exactly ("right on her back")

rainbow.d: an arc of many colors in the sky after rain
rainbow.ex: We saw a rainbow after the rain.

however.ex: I wanted to play. However, it was raining.

instead.ex: I drank water instead of soda.

inhibit.d: to hold someone back; to stop or slow down something
inhibit.ex: The tall fence inhibits the dog from running away.

coil.d: to make round loops, like a rope or a snake
coil.ex: The snake coiled around the branch.

shake.d: to move something quickly up and down or side to side; shook = past of shake
shake.ex: Shake the bottle before you drink.

look.d: to use your eyes to see

deadly.ex: Some snakes have a deadly bite.

complain.d: to say you are not happy about something
complain.ex: He complained that his soup was cold.

owl.d: a bird with big eyes that is awake at night and says "who, who"
owl.ex: The owl sat on a branch at night.

greet.ex: We greet our teacher every morning.

respect.d: a feeling that someone is important and good, so you are polite to them
respect.ex: We show respect to our grandparents.

give.d: to hand something to someone; gave = past of give
give.ex: I gave my friend a present.

even.d: used to say "more than you think"
even.ex: He is even taller than his dad!

behave.d: to act in a good, polite way

assemble.d: to come together in one place; assembled = past of assemble
assemble.ex: All the students assembled in the hall.

timid.ex: The timid puppy hid behind the sofa.

stand.ex: Please stand up and say hello.

standupto.d: to be brave and say no to someone who is mean
standupto.ex: She stood up to the bully and said, "Stop!"

quail.d: a small round bird that lives on the ground
quail.ex: A quail ran under the bush.

whisper.ex: She whispered a secret to her friend.

gobble.ex: The dog gobbled up its food.

lizard.d: a small animal with four short legs, a long tail and dry skin
lizard.ex: A lizard sat on a warm rock.

cry.d: to shout; also to have tears; cried = past of cry

dart.d: to move very fast and suddenly
dart.ex: The fish darted under a rock.

admit.d: to say that something is true, even if it is hard to say

smile.d: to make a happy face with your mouth

new.d: just made or just got; not old

suggest.ex: I suggested we play a game.

yip.d: a short, high sound that a coyote or small dog makes

coyote.d: a wild animal like a small, thin dog that lives in the desert
coyote.ex: The coyote howled at the moon.

bark.d: to make the loud sound a dog makes
bark.ex: The dog barked at the mailman.

guardian.ex: The lifeguard is a guardian of the pool.

form.ex: We formed a circle on the floor.

body.d: all of a person or animal: head, arms, legs and more
body.ex: Exercise is good for your body.

bring.d: to take something with you to a place
bring.ex: Please bring your book to class.

gift.d: a present; also a special talent
gift.ex: I gave my friend a birthday gift.

friend.d: someone you like and play with
friend.ex: My friend and I ride bikes.

clay.d: soft, wet earth that you can shape and then let dry
clay.ex: We made a bowl out of clay.

wet.ex: Wet the sponge before you wash the car.

water.d: the clear liquid in rivers and rain that we drink
water.ex: Drink water when you are thirsty.

spring.d: a place where water comes up from the ground
spring.ex: We drank cool water from a spring.

quickly.ex: She ran quickly to catch the bus.

great.ex: She did her homework with great care.

care.d: when you do something slowly and carefully so it is right

mold.d: to press soft stuff into a shape
mold.ex: We molded the clay into a cat.

leg.d: the long part of the body you stand and walk on

deer.d: a gentle animal with thin legs; the males have antlers
deer.ex: A deer ran into the forest.

branch.d: a part of a tree that grows out like an arm
branch.ex: A bird sat on the branch.

mesquite.d: a small, spiky tree or bush that grows in dry deserts
mesquite.ex: The mesquite bush grows in the desert.

bush.d: a small, low plant with many branches
bush.ex: A rabbit hid behind the bush.

hand.d: to give something to someone with your hand

push.d: to move something away from you with your hands

stick.d: a long, thin piece of wood
stick.ex: The dog found a big stick.

balance.d: to stay steady and not fall
balance.ex: I can balance on one foot.

bluejay.d: a blue bird with a little crest on its head
bluejay.ex: A blue jay sang in the tree.

caw.d: the loud sound a crow or raven makes

croak.d: to make a low, rough sound, like a frog or raven
croak.ex: The frog croaked by the pond.

raven.ex: A raven landed on the fence.

black.d: the darkest color, like the night sky

feather.d: one of the soft, light things that cover a bird

strong.d: having a lot of power in your body
strong.ex: My dad is strong. He can lift me up.

eagle.d: a very big, strong bird that flies high
eagle.ex: An eagle flew over the mountain.

pluck.ex: She plucked a flower from the garden.

dark.ex: The room is dark at night.

wing.d: the part of a bird that it uses to fly

beak.d: the hard, pointy mouth of a bird
beak.ex: The bird picks up seeds with its beak.

peck.d: to hit or bite with a beak
peck.ex: The chicken pecked at the corn.

heron.d: a tall bird with long legs and a long beak that lives near water
heron.ex: A heron stood in the river.

offer.d: to hold out something so someone can take it

thin.ex: The pencil is long and thin.

reed.d: a tall grass with a long, thin stem that grows near water

marsh.d: soft, wet land with tall grass

sharp.d: very good at seeing; also having a point that can cut

eye.d: the part of your face that you see with

stone.ex: We threw stones into the lake.

riverbed.d: the ground at the bottom of a river
riverbed.ex: We found pretty rocks in the riverbed.

add.d: to put one thing with another

bird.d: an animal with feathers and wings
bird.ex: A little bird sang a song.

shape.d: "took shape" = started to look like something
shape.ex: The snowman took shape as we worked.

ask.d: to say a question; asked = past of ask
ask.ex: I asked my teacher a question.

agile.d: able to move quickly and easily

answer.d: to say something back to a question

breathe.d: to take air in and out of your body; "breathed life" = made it alive

life.d: being alive; how someone lives (lives = more than one life)

open.d: to move something so it is not closed

blink.d: to close and open your eyes very fast
blink.ex: The baby blinked in the bright sun.

step.d: when you put one foot in front of the other
step.ex: The baby took her first steps.

totter.d: to walk in a shaky way, almost falling
totter.ex: The baby tottered across the room.

backward.ex: He walked backward and bumped into a chair.

fall.d: to go down to the ground by accident; fell = past of fall

flat.d: lying all the way down; "fell flat on his face" = fell down on his face
flat.ex: He fell flat on the snow.

face.d: the front of your head with eyes, nose and mouth
face.ex: She has a big smile on her face.

sigh.d: to breathe out a long breath when you are sad or tired

head.d: the top part of your body with your eyes, ears and mouth; "shook their heads" = moved heads to say no

awkward.d: moving in a clumsy way, not smooth
awkward.ex: The new puppy is awkward on the stairs.

disappointed.d: sad because something was not as good as you hoped
disappointed.ex: I was disappointed when the picnic was canceled.

learn.d: to get to know something new
learn.ex: I learn new words every day.

really.ex: Can I really go to the zoo?

practice.d: to do something again and again to get better
practice.ex: I practice the piano every day.

try.d: to do your best to do something; tried = past of try
try.ex: I tried to jump over the rope.

cactus.d: a desert plant with sharp spines and thick stems
cactus.ex: Don't touch the cactus. It's sharp!

leap.d: to jump high or far; leaped = past of leap
leap.ex: The frog leaped into the pond.

hornedtoad.d: a small, flat desert lizard with little spikes on its head
hornedtoad.ex: A horned toad sat on the sand.

jump.d: to push yourself up into the air with your legs
jump.ex: The kids jump on the trampoline.

tortoise.d: a slow animal with a hard shell that lives on land

land.d: to come down onto something after jumping or flying

back_n.d: the part of your body behind you, from your neck to your bottom
back_n.ex: The baby rode on my back.

back.d: to the place where you were before

surprised.d: feeling a little shock because something happened that you did not expect
surprised.ex: She was surprised by the party.

turtle.d: an animal with a hard shell; here it means the tortoise
turtle.ex: The turtle hid in its shell.

lumber.ex: The big bear lumbered through the woods.

crash.d: to fall or hit something hard and loudly
crash.ex: The plate crashed to the floor.

ground.ex: The apple fell to the ground.

moan.d: to make a long, sad sound or say something in a sad way

foot.d: the parts at the end of your legs you stand on (one foot, two feet)

skinny.ex: The skinny cat ate a big dinner.

swirl.d: to turn round and round in circles
swirl.ex: The leaves swirled in the wind.

twirl.ex: She twirled in her new dress.

twister.d: a tornado; strong wind that spins very fast
twister.ex: The twister spun across the field.

once.d: before; at a time in the past
once.ex: The once tiny puppy is now a big dog.

graceful.d: moving in a smooth and beautiful way

gracefully.d: in a smooth and beautiful way

get.d: "I've got it!" = I can do it now; I understand
get.ex: "I've got it!" she said after many tries.

zip.ex: The race car zipped past us.

carry.d: to hold something and take it somewhere
carry.ex: I carry my books in my backpack.

swiftly.ex: The rabbit ran swiftly into the woods.

sand.d: tiny bits of rock on beaches and in deserts

thank.d: what you say when someone helps you or gives you something

return.d: to go back; returned = past of return
return.ex: We returned home after the trip.

abode.d: a home; the place where someone lives
abode.ex: The little bird's abode is a nest.

race.ex: The dogs raced across the park.

spy.d: to see something, often from far away; spied = past of spy
spy.ex: I spied a rabbit in the garden.

hide.d: to go where no one can see you
hide.ex: The cat is hiding under the bed.

yucca.d: a desert plant with long, pointy leaves and white flowers
yucca.ex: A yucca plant grows by the road.

plant.d: a living thing that grows in soil and has leaves
plant.ex: My plant needs water every day.

furiously.d: in a very angry and wild way
furiously.ex: The angry baby shook his toy furiously.

everyone.ex: Everyone in my class likes music.

glare.d: to look at someone in an angry way
glare.ex: The cat glared at the dog.

reply.d: to answer; replied = past of reply

hear.d: to get sounds with your ears; heard = past of hear

ruckus.d: a lot of loud noise and trouble
ruckus.ex: The kids made a ruckus in the playroom.

drew.d: to come near; drew = past of draw
drew.ex: The kids drew close to see the puppy.

watch.d: to look at something for some time; "watch out" = be careful
watch.ex: We watch the birds in the garden.

challenge.d: to ask someone to fight or play a game to see who wins
challenge.ex: He challenged me to a race.

show.d: to let someone see something; "I'll show you" = I will prove it

mouse.d: small animals with long tails (one mouse, two mice)

tremble.d: to shake because you are cold or scared
tremble.ex: The puppy trembled in the rain.

fear.ex: She has a fear of spiders.

sound.d: to make a noise that is like something

thunderstorm.d: a storm with rain, thunder and lightning
thunderstorm.ex: We stayed inside during the thunderstorm.

hop.d: to jump in a small way

lunge.d: to jump forward suddenly to get something
lunge.ex: The goalkeeper lunged for the ball.

reach.d: how far you can stretch to touch something; "out of reach" = too far to touch
reach.ex: The cookies are out of reach.

attempt.ex: He made one more attempt to jump the puddle.

lightning.d: a bright flash of light in the sky in a storm

safety.d: a safe place where nothing can hurt you

safe.ex: Wear a helmet to stay safe.

turn.d: the time when it is your chance to do something
turn.ex: It's your turn to roll the dice.

ruffle.d: to make feathers or hair stand up and messy

whirlwind.d: wind that spins round and round very fast
whirlwind.ex: The whirlwind spun the leaves around.

spin.d: to turn around fast; spun = past of spin
spin.ex: The top spun on the table.

serpent.ex: The serpent slid under the rock.

dizzy.d: feeling like everything is turning around you
dizzy.ex: I feel dizzy after the merry-go-round.

crossed.d: "eyes grew crossed" = both eyes looked toward the nose
crossed.ex: The clown made his eyes crossed.

tongue.d: the soft part in your mouth you use to taste

hang.d: to be held at the top and swing down; hung = past of hang
hang.ex: The coat hung on the hook.

limply.d: in a soft, weak way, with no strength

mouth.d: the part of your face you eat and speak with

win.d: to be the best in a game or fight

promise.d: to say that you will really do something
promise.ex: I promise to clean my room.

beat.d: having lost a game or a fight
beat.ex: The beaten team shook hands with the winners.

slink.d: to move away slowly and quietly because you feel bad; slunk = past of slink
slink.ex: The dog slunk away after it ate the cake.

cheer.d: to shout because you are happy

praise.d: to say good things about someone

peace.d: a quiet, calm time with no fighting
peace.ex: The two cats sleep together in peace.

proclaim.d: to say something loudly so everyone hears
proclaim.ex: The mayor proclaimed, "Today is a holiday!"

nolonger.ex: I am no longer a baby.

frightened.ex: The frightened kitten hid under the bed.

wave.d: to move your hand to say hello or goodbye

parent.ex: My parents take me to school.

teach.ex: My mom teaches me to cook.

lesson.d: something you learn; "teach someone a lesson" = make them learn not to do something bad
lesson.ex: He learned a lesson: always wear a coat.

free.d: able to go and do what you want
free.ex: The bird is free to fly.

please.d: "please" = a polite word when you ask; "as they please" = as they want

sure.ex: Make sure you lock the door.

stay.d: to keep being the same; to not leave
stay.ex: Stay safe and wear a helmet.

hadbetter.ex: You had better hurry, or you will miss the bus!

watchout.ex: Watch out! The floor is wet.

say.d: to tell something with words; said = past of say

tell.d: to say something to someone; told = past of tell

make.d: to build or cause something; made = past of make

need.d: to have to have something; you cannot do without it

let.d: to allow; to say "yes, you can"
let.ex: Mom let me stay up late.

first.ex: This is my first lost tooth!

forth.d: first one way, then the other way, many times
forth.ex: The swing goes back and forth.

like.d: the same as; in the same way as

thing.d: an object, or an action or idea; "the right thing" = the right action
thing.ex: Helping Grandma is the right thing to do.
